title: Bean Root Rot (caused by Fusarium) - Rwanda

Header: Bean Root Rot (caused by Fusarium) - Rwanda
Fusarium solani fsp. phaseoli Kinyarwanda: Indwara z’imizi

Prevention: Avoid planting beans in acidic soil (lime application two weeks before planting 5 tonnes per hectare).
Use fertilizers to help plants be more vigorous, basal application organic fertilizer 20-30ton/Ha and
Crop rotation with cereal, root and tuber crops.
Use resistant / tolerant varieties such as
G3331, Vuninkingi (G685), RWV2872, RWV3316, RWV3006, RWR2245, RWR2154.
Do not over irrigate the bean crop.
Monitoring: Monitor the crop once a week from 1 week after seedling emergence up to pod filling stage.
Look for symptoms on hypocotyl and primary root.
On hypocotyl look for tapered red lesions in the lower hypocotyls.
On primary root look for reddish brown lesions 1-2 weeks after seedling emergence.
As infection progresses, the lesions coalesce to become brown and extend up to the soil surface.
Look for longitudinal fissures or cracks on bean stem.
If infection is severe, primary and lateral roots are killed and detached.
On stem, look for stem becoming hollow because of death of primary roots.
Direct Control: Uproot if infected 1-2 weeks after seedling emergence.
Earth up to facilitate formation of new roots that will help the plant to survive. (Earthing up is done after weeding 2-3 weeks after planting).
Restrictions: Do not eat or drink while manipulating pesticide.
